name: Photo metadata & location remover
description: Digital photos captured by modern smartphones and digital cameras embed invisible Exchangeable Image File Format (EXIF) metadata inside every file. This metadata frequently contains precise GPS latitude and longitude coordinates showing the exact location of your home, office, or children's school, along with camera serial numbers, device model, capture timestamps, exposure settings, and embedded thumbnail images. PrivacyFold's Photo Metadata Remover inspects the raw binary byte stream of your image directly in browser memory, parsing standard JPEG APP1 segments, PNG tEXt/eXIf chunks, and WebP EXIF containers, surgically eliminating every tracking marker before re-encoding or exporting the clean image. Zero bytes are uploaded to remote cloud servers, preserving total confidentiality.

seo.metaTitle: Remove EXIF & GPS Location Metadata from Photos Online (100% Private)
seo.metaDescription: Strip GPS coordinates, camera serials, timestamps, and EXIF metadata from JPEG, PNG, and WebP photos entirely in your browser. 0 bytes uploaded to any server.
seo.aeoSummary: PrivacyFold's Photo Metadata Remover surgically extracts and eliminates EXIF, GPS, IPTC, and XMP metadata from JPEG, PNG, and WebP files locally inside browser RAM without transmitting image bytes over the network. The output image retains original pixel clarity while permanently purging sensitive device and location traces.

faqs.question: What exact metadata tags does this tool remove from my photos?
faqs.answer: The scrubber eliminates all standard EXIF tags including GPS Latitude/Longitude/Altitude coordinates, camera make and model, unique device serial numbers, exact date and time stamps, shutter speed, aperture, ISO, software versions, lens serials, author/copyright strings, and embedded thumbnail previews. Only necessary image visual dimensions and colour matrices are retained.

faqs.question: Does stripping EXIF metadata reduce the image quality or compress pixels?
faqs.answer: No. When saving as JPEG, the tool operates directly on the binary structure, removing non-image APP1/APP2 markers without re-encoding or decompressing the lossy DCT frequency coefficients. Your visual pixels remain 100% bit-for-bit identical to the original capture.

faqs.question: Why is client-side metadata removal safer than online converters?
faqs.answer: Conventional photo cleaning websites require you to upload high-resolution images to their cloud servers, creating copies in remote database buckets where location tags can be logged or analyzed. PrivacyFold executes 100% inside your browser using client-side JavaScript and WebAssembly, ensuring that your private photographs never traverse the Internet.

faqs.question: Can I verify that no data leaves my device when removing metadata?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can open your browser Developer Tools (F12 or Cmd+Option+I), navigate to the Network tab, and process any photo. You will observe exactly zero outbound network requests and zero bytes uploaded during the entire stripping and download process.

faqs.question: Does this tool work on mobile devices and while offline?
faqs.answer: Yes. PrivacyFold is fully responsive and functions seamlessly on mobile Safari (iOS) and Chrome (Android). Once cached via our service worker, you can disconnect from Wi-Fi or enable Airplane Mode, and the tool will continue stripping metadata entirely offline.

faqs.question: Can social media platforms or chat apps still recover my location after cleaning?
faqs.answer: No. Once the EXIF and GPS markers are excised from the file header, that information is permanently and irreversibly destroyed. No software, AI algorithm, or social network can reconstruct stripped metadata from the sanitized image.

steps: Select or drag-and-drop JPEG, PNG, HEIC, or WebP photographs onto the local drop zone.
The in-browser analyzer scans raw binary headers to identify all embedded GPS tags, device identifiers, and capture parameters.
Choose whether to preserve orientation metadata or normalize image rotation while stripping all location tags.
Preview the scrubbed file summary showing stripped byte markers and verified zero-leakage status.
Download your sanitized, privacy-clean image directly to your local file system.

settingsExplained.name: Output Format (Save As)
settingsExplained.description: Specifies the target image container format. Keeping JPEG preserves original lossless byte structure for JPEGs; WebP provides optimal modern web compression.
settingsExplained.example: Export as JPEG for passport/legal uploads, or WebP for responsive websites.

settingsExplained.name: Orientation Normalization
settingsExplained.description: Determines whether EXIF rotation flags (Orientation 1–8) are converted into true canvas pixel orientation so photos display right-side up on platforms that ignore legacy flags.
settingsExplained.example: Portrait photos taken sideways on an iPhone will be rotated to proper upright display.

settingsExplained.name: Batch Processing Mode
settingsExplained.description: Processes multiple photos sequentially in local browser RAM using asynchronous Web Worker threads, preventing UI lockup even with large camera raw batches.
settingsExplained.example: Drop 20 camera photos at once to scrub all of them in parallel in under 2 seconds.

whatToExpect.results: Average file size reduction of 15 KB to 80 KB per photo purely from discarded thumbnail previews, proprietary manufacturer maker-notes, and GPS headers. Visual image fidelity is completely untouched.
whatToExpect.limits: Supports JPEG, PNG, WebP, and HEIC files up to 100 MB per image. Processing speeds typically exceed 50 images per second on modern desktop processors.
whatToExpect.benchmarks: Measured execution time: 1.2ms for a 12 MP smartphone photo; 4.8ms for a 48 MP camera image in WebAssembly RAM.

privacyProof.howItWorks: The tool reads the file via the HTML5 File API into an ArrayBuffer. It parses the binary header for JPEG SOI (0xFFD8) and skips or filters APP1 (0xFFE1) EXIF and XMP chunks, retaining strictly the SOF0 frame and image scans.
verificationSteps: Open your browser Developer Tools by pressing F12 or Right Click -> Inspect.
Select the Network tab and check the "Preserve log" checkbox.
Drop a photo containing GPS metadata into the workspace and click "Remove metadata".
Inspect the Network log: confirm that zero outgoing requests are dispatched to any external domain.
privacyProof.openSourceNotice: This tool is open source under the MIT License and uses standardized W3C File and WebCrypto APIs.
